audit_findings.title: Sustaining capital may exceed the amount embedded in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 filed maintenance-and-improvement range of $170 million-$235 million; the upper end is $65.5 million, or 39.8% of the $164.4 million anchor, above 2025 replacement-and-improvement spending of $169.5 million; economically sustaining reserve additions are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A higher recurring sustaining-capital deduction directly reduces anchor owner earnings and every scenario's operating and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: For 2026, we expect capital expenditures for maintenance and improvement to be between $170 million and $235 million and approximately $130 million for organic growth projects and aggregate reserve additions.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that management expects potentially much higher maintenance-and-improvement spending, but it does not demonstrate that the anchor used an inadequate charge because the anchor calculation and economic classification of improvement and reserve spending are absent. The potential annual difference is large relative to owner earnings and is reasonably capable of materially lowering the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $164.4 million anchor to 2025 net income, depreciation/depletion/amortization, the $169.5 million replacement-and-improvement spending, and reserve expenditures. Classify sustaining versus expansion spending asset by asset, then rerun all scenarios with the supported normalized sustaining charge.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement obligations may be an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $78.8 million at December 31, 2025, equal to $1.38 per diluted share and 3.4% of the $2.351 billion base equity value; latest-quarter balance and any uncaptured normalized cash cost are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: An unfunded reclamation obligation belongs either as a claim in the equity bridge or through recurring reclamation cash expenditures deducted from owner earnings, without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, we had total liabilities of $78.8 million related to asset retirement obligations that are excluded from the table above.
audit_findings.explanation: The stated bridge demonstrably omits the filed $78.8 million ARO. It is not yet demonstrated that value is overstated because owner earnings may already capture reclamation settlements or related sustaining expenditures. The balance-sheet claim alone is modest relative to base value, but the record does not establish the latest balance or whether depreciation added back in owner earnings removed costs needed to settle it.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 ARO balance and rollforward, trace the $2.1 million of 2025 settlements and related capital spending through the owner-earnings calculation, and rerun using either normalized cash settlements in owner earnings or the net unfunded ARO in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Portland Harbor creates an unquantified environmental tail claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Any uninsured or unindemnified company allocation would reduce equity through a bridge claim or future remediation cash outflows not included in owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: This remedy, which will not begin until the EPA has approved remedial design and remedial action plans from the PRPs, was expected to require 13 years of active remediation and cost $ 1 billion to $ 2 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The $1 billion-$2 billion estimate is for the entire site and cannot be treated as Knife River's exposure. Knife River's allocation, natural-resource damages, and indemnity recovery remain unresolved. The June 2026 filing reported no material change and management does not expect material costs, but that does not quantify the company's share or prove the indemnity will perform. This is an existing contingent claim, not merely a forward-looking operating risk.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the current PRP allocation and mediation materials, remedial-design cost updates, natural-resource-damage assessment, and the Linnton sale agreement. Test the Georgia-Pacific indemnity's scope, enforceability, and counterparty credit, then rerun the bridge for the supported net exposure.

audit_findings.title: Owner earnings may omit material working-capital requirements
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 cash used by working-capital components increased $74.8 million, equal to 45.5% of the $164.4 million anchor; normalized recurring requirement is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring increases in receivables, contract assets, and inventory, net of operating liabilities, reduce distributable owner earnings and therefore operating and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash used by working capital components increased $74.8 million in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a large cash use but attributes part of it to acquisitions, taxes, software timing, and payment timing, so it does not demonstrate that the full $74.8 million is recurring or omitted from owner earnings. If the owner-earnings series excludes normalized incremental working capital, the potential scale is material relative to the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each owner-earnings year to the cash-flow statement and separately identify acquisition balances, seasonal reversals, tax and payment timing, and structural working-capital growth. Rerun all scenarios with the supported normalized recurring requirement.

audit_findings.title: The perimeter analysis omits four 2025 acquisitions
audit_findings.magnitude: $177.2 million aggregate purchase consideration for the four omitted acquisitions, equal to 7.5% of the $2.351 billion base equity value; their earnings contribution and full-year uplift are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Partial-year acquired earnings affect the owner-earnings anchor and the amount of acquisition-related growth that should be recognized after the anchor year.
audit_findings.evidence: In 2025, we successfully completed the acquisition and integration of five companies expanding our footprint within existing markets, which was an investment of $611.7 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter-documentation error: the valuation names only Strata although the filing reports five 2025 acquisitions. It is not yet a demonstrated valuation error because the as-filed anchor automatically includes each acquisition from its closing date. Value could be understated if the forecast omits their full-year economics, or overstated if those economics are already embedded in the growth assumptions and credited again.
audit_findings.action: List all five closing dates, acquired and disposed operations, and post-closing revenue and owner-earnings contributions. Build a perimeter schedule and rerun only after determining whether the existing growth paths omit or duplicate the four acquisitions' full-year economics.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded benefit promises require a net-claim reconciliation
audit_findings.magnitude: identified gross obligations of $29.969 million, comprising a $13.747 million nonqualified defined-benefit obligation and $16.222 million other-postretirement obligation, equal to $0.52 per diluted share and 1.3% of the $2.351 billion base equity value; designated investments were $44.399 million and the complete net amount is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Benefit liabilities reduce the equity bridge, while genuinely available designated investments increase it; cash benefit payments also affect owner earnings if accounting expense replaces cash cost.
audit_findings.evidence: Subsequent to the Separation, the unfunded, nonqualified defined benefit plans in which we participate are single employer plans for executive officers and certain key management employees.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge lacks a documented net reconciliation, but even charging the identified $29.969 million gross obligations with no credit for designated investments would reduce base value by only about $0.52 per share. That is small against the $20.76 gap between the $41.07 base value and the $61.83 market price and the $12.94 gap even under the bull case, so the disclosed claims cannot change the valuation conclusion. The direction is mixed because the bridge omits both obligations and potentially offsetting assets.
audit_findings.action: Document the June 30, 2026 nonqualified defined-benefit, defined-contribution, and postretirement liabilities; match them to legally and economically available insurance and investment assets; and confirm cash benefit payments in owner earnings. Rerun only if the reconciliation uncovers additional net claims materially exceeding the disclosed gross scale.
